These outputs were worked out by hand. For an all-equal array of length n, every valid index tuple works, and the valid tuples correspond to choosing 4 of the n−3 usable positions, giving C(n−3, 4). For length 7 the only possible tuple is (0,2,4,6), which is why several length-7 cases give 0 or 1. The mixed 1/2 array of length 8 has exactly three valid tuples: (0,2,4,6), (0,2,5,7) and (1,3,5,7).
